content: Sodium propionate, also known as sodium propanoate, is the sodium salt derived from propionic acid. Its chemical formula is Na(C2H5COO). This compound appears as a white crystalline solid and exhibits deliquescent properties, meaning it absorbs moisture from the air. Sodium propionate is synthesized through a chemical reaction between propionic acid and either sodium carbonate or sodium hydroxide. This compound is widely utilized as a food preservative and is identified by the food labeling E number E281 in Europe. Its primary application is as a mold inhibitor, particularly in bakery products. Sodium propionate has been approved for use as a food additive in the European Union, the United States, Australia, and New Zealand, where it is recognized by its International Numbering System (INS) designation, 281.
